title: The Two Doors
text: Two doors stand in a hillside, one guarded by a knight who always lies and one by a knight who never does. It is the usual riddle, and the knights look bored. Their armor is very old, and nothing moves behind their visors.

options.label: The wisest asks the riddle's question, as it has always been asked.

outcomes.text: They choose the right door, which proves a short way. The knights clap politely.

options.label: Fight your way past the nearer knight; riddles are for the bored.

outcomes.text: They are not bored any more.

options.label: The Leader picks a door at random, trusting to luck.
